samples.question: The picture shows a wiring diagram on white paper. Grey wires of equal thickness join only where they meet at a junction, and no two wires cross anywhere in the picture, so wires that merely pass near each other are not joined. Exactly one wire is drawn in violet instead of grey. A red, a blue and a green dot each sit on a junction of the wiring, and no dot sits on an end of the violet wire. Now imagine erasing the violet wire completely while leaving every grey wire and both of its end junctions in place. After that erasure, two dots count as connected only if you can travel from one to the other along grey wire the whole way, never jumping a gap. Once the violet wire is erased, which dots are still connected to each other? Answer 'red and blue', 'red and green', 'blue and green', or 'all three'.
